summary: The reference patch implements every manual TD-7 rule (week's-pay crediting, 13-week base period divided by thirteen, two-thirds rate with the row in force on the injury date, the low-wage rule, inclusive disability days, a three-day waiting period, retroactive days from fourteen, TTD rounded to the nearest cent, two-thirds partial benefit capped at the rate). Where no manual rule reaches (a line under 2,000 cents keeps its payday's week; a partial week under 1,000 cents keeps the shipped 3/5 share, capped at the rate), it keeps today's calculation, as instruction.md paragraph 2 requires. The patch hunks match the shipped files, and the driver is not touched. No concrete incorrect behavior found.
checks_performed: Checked every fix.patch hunk header and its context lines against the shipped disability.py, partial.py, payroll.py and rates.py line numbers; all hunks line up (solve.sh applies them with patch -p1 from /, and the Dockerfile installs patch).

Traced wage-line crediting: a Friday line of 2,000 cents or more goes to week_ending(Friday) - 7 = the Sunday five days earlier (manual 2.2/3.1). A smaller line stays on the payday's week, which is today's step, because 3.2 only says 'one payroll week' (instruction.md:3).
Traced the AWW. It is half_up(base wages, 13) (3.3); with no base-period lines it gives 0. This also removes the shipped divide-by-zero when weeks_paid is 0.

Traced the weekly rate. The row in force is the last row taking effect on or before the injury date, starting from table[0], which 1.3 guarantees applies (2.4). An AWW below the minimum returns the AWW (3.5). Otherwise the rate is 2/3 of the AWW rounded half-up, then clamped to max and min (3.4). Division by 3 never leaves an exact half, and clamping to integer bounds makes the round-then-clamp order irrelevant.

Traced disability days: (last - first).days + 1 (2.5); waiting = min(3, days) (2.6); retro = waiting when days >= 14 (4.1); paid = days - waiting + retro (4.2); ttd = half_up(rate * paid, 7) (4.3 with 1.1, and 7 is odd, so there is no half).

Traced partial disability: wage loss = aww - earned, or 0 (2.7). A week earning 1,000 cents or more pays 2/3 of its loss, capped at the rate (2.8/5.1). A week earning less pays the shipped 3/5 of its loss, capped at the rate. The manual gives no share for such weeks, while 5.2 still gives them a benefit, and instruction.md:3 keeps the package constants at today's values. tpd_weeks = len(earnings) (6.1).
Checked the statement keys and order and the total = ttd + tpd against README.md and manual 6.1. Every figure is a Python int, and statements come out in job order.

Checked that model.py agrees with the patch on each step, including counted_week (Friday - 5 days) and the 3/5 low-week share. This was a consistency check only, not an independent correctness argument.

Hand-traced the sample job: 2025-03-12 is a Wednesday, so the base period runs from Sunday 2024-12-01 to Sunday 2025-03-02. The 2024-12-06 week's pay credits to 2024-12-01 (in the base period). The 2025-03-07 week's pay credits to 2025-03-02 (in). The 2025-03-14 line is in the injury week (out). The 37-cent correction stays on Sunday 2025-01-26 (in). The row in force is the 2024-07-01 row.

coverage_sweep.category: Trace an ordinary case and each relevant boundary through the reference logic
coverage_sweep.reason: Traced the ordinary sample claim and these boundaries: a line of exactly 2,000 and of 1,999 cents; injury on a Monday, Friday or Sunday; zero base-period lines; AWW at or below the minimum; 2/3 AWW at the max or min; 1-, 2-, 3-, 13- and 14-day disability; TTD remainders 1-6 sevenths; partial weeks of 999, 1,000, the AWW and more than the AWW.

coverage_sweep.category: Output bytes: widths, precision, types, keys, paths
coverage_sweep.reason: All figures are integer cents from integer arithmetic (half_up), with exactly the README keys in FIELDS order. The claim string passes through unchanged, and the driver is unchanged, as instruction.md requires.

coverage_sweep.category: State-updating branches (loop state, replacement, identifier reuse)
coverage_sweep.reason: The only loop state is row_in_force's 'chosen', which is reset per call and seeded with table[0], and the per-claim tpd/wage accumulators, which are local per call. No carry-over between claims.

coverage_sweep.category: Recovery and durability claims at interruption points
coverage_sweep.reason: The contract is a pure computation from a job file to stdout, with no recovery or durability promises.

Rounding is half-up to the nearest cent only where a rule multiplies or divides: AWW /13, rate x2/3, TTD /7, partial x2/3 or x3/5. The base-period sum and the total are not rounded. None of the odd divisors can produce an exact half.

coverage_sweep.category: Unreached-rule fallback required by instruction.md paragraph 2
coverage_sweep.reason: Two gaps keep today's step. A sub-2,000-cent line keeps the payday's week. A partial week under 1,000 cents keeps the shipped 3/5 share with the shipped cap, fed by the manual AWW and rate. No added guard or clamp.

interaction_sweep.case_or_path: A week's pay on the Friday of the injury week credits to the last base week (included). A week's pay on the Friday after the first base week credits to the first base week (included). A week's pay for the week before the base period is excluded.

A sub-2,000-cent correction on the injury-week Friday stays on the injury week and is excluded. One on the first base week's Friday stays on that week and is included. This is today's placement, as instruction.md:3 requires.

rules: 5.1 partial cap at the weekly rate
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: AWW 30,000 with min 45,000 gives rate 30,000. A partial week earning 15,000 has a loss of 15,000, 2/3 of which is 10,000, under the 30,000 cap, so it pays 10,000.
An injury the day before a row change uses the earlier row's max and min. An injury on the change day uses the new row. The clamp uses the chosen row.

rules: 4.1 retroactive at fourteen days over multiple periods
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: Periods [5,4,5], counted inclusively, give 14 days: waiting 3, retro 3, paid 14. A single 13-day period gives waiting 3, retro 0, paid 10.

rules: 2.7 wage loss nought at or above AWW
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: A week earning 999 cents with AWW 999 or less has loss 0 regardless of share. A week earning the AWW or more has loss 0. A week of 1,000 cents uses 2/3 and a week of 999 uses 3/5.
No wage lines gives AWW 0, which is below the minimum (at least 1,000), so the rate is 0 and TTD is 0. No division by zero after the patch.
